reasoning: Quadriliteral verb with two emphatic ض, both capital D. Everyday Palestinian for pouring your heart out.
Plural imperative ta3aalu; عند plus -na contracts to 3inna, which is how Palestinians say at our place.
Active participle baarid, used of food and drink that is cold, and of a cold-mannered person.
ث comes out as a plain t in Palestinian, so respelled تانوية. The -iyye ending has a doubled ya. Full term is madrase taanawiyye.
Both words have long ee in Palestinian: gheer heek. غ is gh.
Urban Palestinian has no interdental ذ, so it is a plain d and the Arabic is respelled بادنجان. baTinjaan and bitinjaan are widely heard variants.
ق is a glottal stop in this everyday spice word, and taa marbuta after ف is e.
ض is emphatic D. Accurate but slightly clinical; in a house people say shaash for gauze and laz'a for a sticking plaster.
Bound preposition that takes pronoun suffixes: ili, ilak, ilha, as in haad ili for that is mine. The initial hamza sits on an alif seat so only the vowel is written.
biddi is the Palestinian want, followed by a bare subjunctive. ص is emphatic S and the vowel in aSbugh is u.
Damma in the first syllable and taa marbuta after ب as e: rukbe.
The short vowel of the participle drops in Palestinian: 3aaSfe, not 3aaSifa. ص is emphatic and taa marbuta after ف is e.
Past 3ms 7akam. The same form also means judged or refereed, but ruled over is a correct sense.
Verbs negate with ما. Both ق are glottal stops: ba'dar, al7a'. لحق here is to make it in time.
Imperative ruu7 to a man, then bi- plus the article assimilated to the sun letter س. Taa marbuta after م is e.
An ordinary everyday word, so the ق glottalises: 'aamuus. Careful or classroom speech keeps qaamuus.
The first short vowel drops in Palestinian, giving an initial cluster: rkhiiS, with emphatic S.
Weather is framed with id-dinya plus a noun, literally the world is cold. The article assimilates to د.
عبّى is form II with shadda on ب: a3abbi. banziin is the Palestinian word for petrol.
b-present 2ms with the 3fs object suffix, then the Palestinian disjunction walla and the negative la' with a final glottal stop.
Two kasras in Palestinian, kitif, not MSA katif.

Ramallah says jaaje for one chicken, with the د of دجاجة gone, so the Arabic is respelled جاجة; djaaje is also heard. Taa marbuta after ج is e.

MSA-derived connector that educated Ramallah speakers do use, with the Palestinian demonstrative haad rather than هذا. The article assimilates to ن; ظ is TH, though many speakers say an emphatic z here.
